title: Single-area OSPF with three routers
summary: Bring up OSPF neighbours and learn every network on every router.
objectives: Start OSPF and give each router a unique router ID
Advertise the right networks in area 0
Form neighbour relationships on both links
Learn every remote network on every router

tasks.title: Start OSPF with unique router IDs
tasks.description: Start OSPF process 1 on every router. Use router IDs 1.1.1.1 (R1), 2.2.2.2 (R2) and 3.3.3.3 (R3).
hints: Two routers with the same router ID will not become neighbours.
In system view, the router ID goes on the same line as the process number.
Example on R1: system-view, then ospf 1 router-id 1.1.1.1

tasks.title: Advertise the connected networks
tasks.description: Put every connected network in area 0. A network statement uses a wildcard mask, the inverse of the subnet mask (a /30 is 0.0.0.3, a /25 is 0.0.0.127).
hints: R1 has two networks to advertise: the link to R2 (192.0.2.0/30) and its LAN (203.0.113.0/25).
A router only forms a neighbour on a link whose address is covered by one of its network statements.

Example on R1: ospf 1 area 0 network 192.0.2.0 0.0.0.3 and ospf 1 area 0 network 203.0.113.0 0.0.0.127. R2 has the two link networks (192.0.2.0/30 and 198.51.100.0/30). R3 has 198.51.100.0/30 and 203.0.113.128/25.

criteria.label: R1 and R2 are OSPF neighbours
R2 and R3 are OSPF neighbours

tasks.title: Learn every network
tasks.description: Each router must learn, through OSPF, the networks it is not directly connected to.
hints: If a route is missing, a LAN network statement is probably missing on the router that owns that LAN.
R1 and R3 each own a LAN; R2 must learn both of them.
